is_anopheles.evidence: The study exclusively focuses on Aedes aegypti, as stated in the title 'Genetic Diversity of Brazilian Aedes aegypti: Patterns following an Eradication Program' and throughout the text.

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study genotypes 12 neutral microsatellite loci to assess population structure, and does not genotype any of the target insecticide resistance markers.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No genotype or allele counts/frequencies for any target insecticide resistance markers are reported.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from Brazil, Venezuela, Mexico, USA, Dominica, and Puerto Rico (Table 1), none from Africa.

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study analyzing microsatellite variation in Aedes aegypti populations.

sub_country_location.evidence: Collection sites in Brazil are specified with coordinates and municipalities, e.g., 'Aracaju, Sergipe, Brazil' (-10.909151, -37.074454) in Table 1.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collection years are provided per site (e.g., 2008, 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012/2013) in Table 1.

duplicate_risk.evidence: Not applicable as this study is outside the scope of African Anopheles surveillance.

supplement.evidence: No relevant data for our database would be present in the supplements, as the species and markers are entirely out of scope.

assessment.summary: This study analyzes the population genetic structure and recolonization history of Aedes aegypti in Brazil using 12 microsatellite markers across 11 Brazilian locations and several comparison populations in the Americas and Caribbean.
exclusion_reasons: Study organism is Aedes aegypti, not Anopheles mosquitoes.
Mosquitoes were collected in the Americas/Caribbean, not Africa.
Does not genotype any target insecticide resistance markers (analyzed microsatellite loci only).
